title: Luca Dellanna VALUEx BRK 2026
description:
Why Habits Beat Incentives 
Hungary spends nearly 5% of GDP on family-formation incentives without moving fertility. Why habits outperform incentives across business, sport, and life.

See the full stream of the event here: https://youtube.com/live/V3V7bqLGP9o
summary: The speaker argues that high performance and repeated behaviors are driven by habits and competence rather than financial incentives alone, noting that incentives often fail to solve habit problems or create great performers from those lacking the right foundations. He illustrates this principle with examples ranging from wallet-finding scenarios and Cristiano Ronaldo's training to corporate successes at Ryanair and Toyota, concluding that immediate feedback and building competence are the most reliable methods for establishing lasting habits.
